Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS India, South Korea Sign Pact to Boost Skill Development in Shipbuilding Sector On April 2 2026, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) signed a Plan of Implementation (PoI) with South Korea’s Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) in New Delhi (Delhi) to enhance skill development in India’s shipbuilding and maritime sector. • The agreement aligns with the objectives of the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision (MAKV) 2047, aimed at strengthening India’s global maritime position. Exam Hint: ✓ What? Plan of Implementation (PoI) for skill development in shipbuilding ✓ Signed between: India (MoPSW) & South Korea (KOICA) ✓ Focus Areas: Workforce mapping, skill gap assessment, human resource roadmap ✓ Support Agency: KRIVET ✓ Key Initiative: Bilateral workshops (India & South Korea) ✓ Proposal: Shipbuilding Workforce Development & Technology Cooperation Center in India ✓ Aligned with: Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision (MAKV) 2047. About Plan of Implementation (PoI): Objective: The project, titled ‘Support the Establishment of Development Strategies and to Build a Foundation for Skilled and Professional Talents for the Indian Shipbuilding and Marine Sector,’ aims to modernize the workforce to support economic growth. Key Focus Areas: Under this collaboration, KOICA, along with the Korea Research Institute for Vocational Education and Training (KRIVET), will conduct research on India’s shipbuilding and marine engineering sectors. • It will focus on workforce mapping, skill gap assessment, and developing a structured human resource roadmap. Implementation: A series of bilateral workshops will be conducted in India and South Korea with participation from industry experts, policymakers, and academic institutions. • These workshops will facilitate knowledge sharing and strengthen bilateral cooperation. Capacity Building: The focus is on building a future-ready maritime workforce and generating high-quality employment for the youth under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. Dedicated Technology Center: Discussions are in the final stages to establish a Shipbuilding Workforce Development and Technology Cooperation Center in India, aimed at strengthening the sector. • The centre will provide industry-oriented vocational training and enhance technical competencies for the modern shipbuilding ecosystem. About South Korea: President- Lee Jae Myung Capital- Seoul Currency- South Korean Won (KRW) MoE Declares NCERT as ‘Deemed to be University’ Under Distinct Category On 30th March 2026, the Ministry of Education (MoE), through its Department of Higher Education (DHE), declared the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) as a ‘Deemed to be University’ under a distinct category as per Section 3 of the University Grants Commission (UGC) Act, 1956. • This marks a significant structural shift in India’s educational landscape, strengthening teacher education and research in alignment with the goals of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

# Page 22^page=22
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 22 Daily Content PDF Exam Hints: ✓ What? Declared as Deemed to be University ✓ Entity: NCERT ✓ By Whom? Department of Higher Education, MoE ✓ Category: Distinct category (Earlier De-Novo) ✓ Act: UGC Act, 1956 (Section 3) ✓ Units Covered: 6 constituent institutes: RIEs at Ajmer, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Mysuru, Shillong; Pandit Sunderlal Sharma Central Institute of Vocational Education, Bhopal ✓ Key conditions: No commercial activities, no fund diversion, NAAC/NBA accreditation, NIRF participation, ABC integration, Samarth e-Governance ✓ Alignment: NEP 2020. NCERT Deemed-to-be-University Status: Background: The transition followed a multi-year process starting with a Letter of Intent in August 2023, requiring NCERT to meet specified conditions, with a compliance report submitted in November 2025, accepted by a UGC expert committee, and approved by the commission. DeNovo: Three years prior, the Government of India(GoI) approved NCERT’s deemed-to-be-university status in the ‘De-Novo‘ category, which allows institutions to apply to the UGC to set up new universities focused on unique and emerging areas of knowledge not offered by existing institutions. NCERT Constituent Units: Constituents: The status covers NCERT along with six of its constituent institutions across India includes: Regional Institute of Education (RIE), Ajmer (Rajasthan); RIE, Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh, MP); RIE, Bhubaneswar (Odisha); RIE, Mysuru (Karnataka) ; North East RIE, Shillong (Meghalaya); Pandit Sunderlal Sharma Central Institute of Vocational Education (PSSCIVE), Bhopal (MP). Affiliation: Previously affiliated with Barkatullah University, MDS University, University of Mysore, Utkal University, and North-Eastern Hill University; no longer requires parent university approval for new courses. Academic: NCERT can now offer Diploma, Undergraduate (UG), Postgraduate (PG), Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), and specialised programmes while continuing curriculum development. Compliance and Conditions: Funds: NCERT shall not divert assets or funds without prior permission from the UGC and Central Government, and must not engage in commercial or profit-making activities. Standards & Accreditation: Academic programmes must comply with UGC and statutory norms, and obtain accreditation from the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) and the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) for eligible courses. Digital: NCERT must implement the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) for students, upload credit data in digital lockers, integrate with the ABC portal, and adopt the Samarth e-Governance platform. Regulation: Admissions, intake, and course approvals continue under UGC regulations, the Memorandum of Association (MoA) must be updated, and NCERT must participate in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF). Expansion: NCERT is directed to broaden its role, focusing on research, teacher education, and innovation in school education. About National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT): NCERT is an autonomous organisation that plays a crucial role in shaping school education in India. It assists and advises both Central and State governments on policies, develops curricula, and publishes textbooks and learning materials.

# Page 25^page=25
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 25 Daily Content PDF Pilot States: Nine states participate in the BIS pilot: Andhra Pradesh (AP), Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh (MP), Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh (UP). Borrowing Volume: The nine pilot states are projected to borrow Rs 1,53,900 crore under BIS, while remaining states and Union Territories (UTs) will raise Rs 1,00,609 crore through traditional market borrowing methods. Role: As debt manager, the RBI schedules regular auctions and can adjust dates or amounts in consultation with states to prevent market volatility. Significance: The BIS provides a structured borrowing strategy that strengthens market stability, improves investor planning, and enhances transparency in public finance. About the Reserve Bank of India (RBI): Establishment: RBI was established on 1st April 1935 based on the Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommendations and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, initially in Calcutta (now Kolkata, West Bengal) and permanently moved to Mumbai, Maharashtra in 1937, before being nationalised in 1949 and joining the Asian Clearing Union (ACU). Governance: Managed by a 21-member Central Board of Directors (CBD) appointed by the Government of India (GoI), including the Governor Sanjay Malhotra (26th) and 4 Deputy Governors: T. Rabi Sankar, Swaminathan J., Dr. Poonam Gupta, and Shirish Chandra Murmu. Functions: Serves as the national monetary authority, manages currency issuance and exchange, acts as banker and debt manager to the Central and State Governments, regulates banks and financial institutions, and oversees foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 to maintain price stability, support growth, and safeguard the Indian Rupee. Headquarters- Mumbai, Maharashtra CASA Ratio Falls to 2-Year Low of 37.9% in Dec 2025 Quarter: RBI Data In April 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that the share of Current Account and Savings Account (CASA) deposits in total bank deposits declined to a 2-year low of 37.9% in December 2025 quarter, compared to 40.1% in December 2023. • CASA ratio refers to the proportion of low-cost deposits (current and savings accounts) in a bank’s total deposits. Exam Hints ✓ What? CASA ratio declined to 37.9% (2-year low) ✓ When? December 2025 quarter ✓ Reason: Shift towards equities, MF & gold ✓ Savings Share: 28.9% ✓ Total Deposits: Rs 239.8 lakh crore ✓ CD Issuance: Rs 15.5 lakh crore (FY26) Banking Trends: Savings Decline: The decline was mainly driven by savings accounts, whose share fell by 210 basis points to 28.9%, as depositors shifted to higher-yielding options like equities, Mutual Funds (MF), and gold, indicating a slowdown in deposit mobilisation. Deposit Growth: Bank deposits grew 10% Year-on-Year (YoY) to Rs 239.8 lakh crore, with savings deposits rising 8% to Rs 69.4 lakh crore and current account deposits increasing 10% to Rs 21.4 lakh crore. CD Issuance: Certificates of Deposit (CD) issuances by banks reached a record Rs. 15.5 lakh crore in Financial Year 2025-26(FY26), up 17% YoY, as lenders increasingly relied on market borrowings to support credit growth.

# Page 26^page=26
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 26 Daily Content PDF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY Indian Navy Commissions Third Nuclear-Powered Ballistic Missile Submarine INS Aridhaman In April 2026, Indian Navy (IN) commissioned its third indigenously built Ship, Submersible, Ballistic, Nuclear (SSBN), ‘Indian Naval Ship (INS) Aridhaman (S4)’, at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh (AP). • The ceremony was presided over by Union Minister Rajnath Singh, Ministry of Defence (MoD), who also laid the foundation stone for a state-of-the-art Large Cavitation Tunnel (LCT). Exam Hint: ✓ What? Commissioning of 3rd Ship, Submersible, Ballistic, Nuclear (SSBN) ✓ Name of Submarine: INS Aridhaman (S4) ✓ Where? Visakhapatnam, AP ✓ Ceremony Presided over by: Rajnath Singh, MoD ✓ Project: Advanced Technology Vessel ✓ Class: Arihant-class (after INS Arihant & INS Arighaat) ✓ Key Features: ✓ 7,000 tonnes | ~130 m length ✓ 83 MW nuclear reactor (BARC) ✓ Speed: ~24 knots ✓ Indigenisation: ~70% (USHUS & Panchendriya SONAR) ✓ Other Event: Foundation laid for Large Cavitation Tunnel ✓ Location: NSTL, Visakhapatnam ✓ Agency: DRDO ✓ Purpose: Hydrodynamic testing, noise reduction & stealth enhancement. About INS Aridhaman: Overview: INS Aridhaman is constructed under the Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project at Visakhapatnam. It belongs to the Arihant class, following INS Arihant (2016) and INS Arighaat (2024), and features enhanced capacity for submarine-launched ballistic missiles, with most technical specifications remaining classified. Construction Timeline: The vessel was laid down in 2018 and subsequently launched on 23 November 2021. Builder: The ship was constructed at the Shipbuilding Centre (SBC), Visakhapatnam. Dimensions: The submarine has a length of approximately 130 metre(m) and a displacement of 7,000 tonnes, making it larger and more potent than its predecessors. Propulsion: It is powered by an indigenous 83 MW Compact Light Water Reactor (CLWR) developed by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), enabling submerged speeds of up to 24 knots. Weaponry: Equipped with eight vertical launch tubes, it can carry either 8 K-4 Intermediate-Range Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missiles (SLBMs) with a 3,500 kilometre (km) range or 24 K-15 Sagarika short-range SLBMs with a 750 km range. Indigenous Content: The vessel features approximately 70% indigenous content, including the USHUS Integrated Submarine SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) and the Panchendriya SONAR suite. About India’s SSBN Fleet (Project Varsha): Operational Status: With the commissioning of S4, India now operates three SSBNs. The fourth vessel, S4(Arisudan), is undergoing sea trials for a 2027 commissioning. Future Roadmap: IN aims to commission its first indigenous nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSNs) by 2036-2037.

# Page 27^page=27
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF Global Standing: India is among the six countries with SSBN capability: United States of America(USA), Russia, United Kingdom(UK), France and China, and is the only nation outside the P5 (UN Security Council Permanent Members) to possess this capability. About Large Cavitation Tunnel (LCT): Union Minister Rajnath Singh also laid the foundation stone for a state-of-the-art Large Cavitation Tunnel (LCT) at the Naval Science & Technological Laboratory (NSTL) in Visakhapatnam. • Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, and Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief (FOC-in-C), Eastern Naval Command Vice Admiral Sanjay Bhalla, along with other senior officials, were present on the occasion. Implementing Agency: The project is a premier initiative of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). Objective: The LCT aims to eliminate dependence on foreign testing facilities for hydrodynamic research, supporting the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative in naval technology. Function: A cavitation tunnel is used to study water flow around ship hulls and propellers. It simulates high-speed conditions to reduce cavitation, the formation of vapor bubbles that create noise and damage propellers. Unique Design: The facility is globally unique for its ability to conduct both closed-loop simulations (for submarines) and free surface simulations (for surface ships) in a single setup. Platform Support: The facility will validate designs for Aircraft Carriers, Destroyers, and next-generation underwater platforms. About Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO): Chairman – Samir V. Kamat Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – January 1, 1958 ISRO Launches ‘Mission MITRA’ in Ladakh to Test Crew Safety for Human Spaceflight In April 2026, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched ‘Mission MITRA (Mapping of Interoperable Traits & Reliability Assessment)’, a high-altitude analogue mission from Leh, Ladakh, conducted between April 2 and 9, 2026, to gather vital data on crew performance and human factors for India’s Gaganyaan program and future long-duration space missions. • The initiative, led by ISRO’s Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC) in collaboration with Protoplanet Private Limited, aims to simulate space-like conditions to study team behavior, resilience, and communication for India’s Gaganyaan crew. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Mission MITRA ✓ By Whom? ISRO with Protoplanet Pvt. Ltd. ✓ Where? Leh, Ladakh ✓ When? April 2–9, 2026 ✓ Altitude: 3,500 metres ✓ Purpose: Study crew performance, behaviour & decision-making under stress for Gaganyaan ✓ Crew Participants: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla; Ajith Krishnan; Angad Pratap; P. Balakrishnan Nair. Key Details of Test: Objective: Mission MITRA is a week-long high-altitude exercise testing physiological, psychological, and operational performance under extreme cold, low oxygen (hypoxia), and isolation, with a multidisciplinary team monitoring safety and generating data for future human spaceflight. Crew: Four Gaganyaan astronaut-designates, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, Ajith Krishnan, Angad

Operational Interoperability: This study is targeted to generate vital understanding on the team inter- operability between crew (gaganyatris) and ground control teams and effectiveness of decision making under environmental and operational stress. Significance: The mission builds on previous analogue exercises and supports India’s long-term goal of a crewed lunar landing by 2040. About Mission MITRA: Design: Mission MITRA is a first-of-its-kind team behavioral study designed jointly by the ISRO and the Indian Air Force (IAF) – Institute of Aerospace Medicine (IAM). Entity: M/s Protoplanet Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru (Karnataka), an Indian start-up, managed facility operations, logistics, and statutory protocols for the mission. About Indian Space Research Organisation(ISRO): Chairman- Dr. V. Narayanan Headquarters- Bengaluru, Karnataka Established- 1969 SPORTS Khelo India Tribal Games 2026 Held in Chhattisgarh; Karnataka Tops with 38 Medals The inaugural Khelo India Tribal Games 2026 (KITG 2026) concluded in Chhattisgarh, held across Raipur, Jagdalpur, and Surguja from 25 March to 3 April 2026, with Karnataka emerging as the overall champion by winning 38 medals, including 23 gold, 8 silver, and 7 bronze. • Odisha secured second position with a total of 57 medals (21 gold, 15 silver, and 21 bronze), while Jharkhand finished third with a total of 35 medals (16 gold, 8 silver, and 11 bronze). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Inaugural Khelo India Tribal Games 2026 held ✓ When? 25 March to 3 April, 2026 ✓ Where? Chhattisgarh (Raipur, Jagdalpur, and Surguja) ✓ Sports: 7 – Archery, Athletics, Football, Hockey, Swimming, Weightlifting, and Wrestling ✓ Winner: Karnataka (23 gold, 8 silver, and 7 bronze) ✓ Runner-ups: Odisha (2nd) & Jharkhand (3rd) ✓ Organiser: MoYAS, SAI, IOA, NSFs, and the Chhattisgarh State Organising Committee. ✓ Mascot: Morveer ✓ Scholarship: Rs. 5 lakh per year for 8 years under the Khelo India Scheme. Evolution of Army Medical Corps (AMC): Origin: The Indian Medical Service (IMS), established in 1612 under the British East India Company. Development: Military medical services were formalized in 1764 with Presidency Medical Services, including Bengal Medical Service (1764), Madras Medical Service (1767), and Bombay Medical Service (1779) for the three Presidency Armies. Amalgamation: During World War II, the Indian Hospital Corps (IHC) formed in 1939, and along with the Indian Medical Service (IMS) and Indian Medical Department (IMD), merged to create the Indian Army Medical Corps (IAMC) on 3 April 1943. Headquarters: The administrative headquarters of the Indian Army Medical Corps (IAMC) was established in Pune, Maharashtra in May 1943. Renaming: After independence, the Indian Army Medical Corps (IAMC) was renamed as the Army Medical Corps (AMC) on 26 January 1950.
